claim: Thomas A. Carlson's paper "Defense First: A Multi-Asset Tactical Model for Adaptive Downside Protection" is listed in the SSRN Electronic Journal as a 2025 preprint (DOI 10.2139/ssrn.5334772); the full abstract and methodology text were not retrievable through the available fetch tooling (only bibliographic metadata rendered), so this iteration's exact-rules pinning relies on the AllocateSmartly and Quantitativo replications and the author's own LinkedIn summary instead of the primary PDF text.
quote: SSRN Electronic Journal. Published: 2025-01-01. Preprint. 0 citations.
limitations: Only a short bibliographic stub (509 bytes: title, author, date, journal, 0 citations) rendered; the fetch tool could not retrieve the abstract or full text of papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5334772 or ssrn.com/abstract=5334772 directly (both attempted, both returned 0 chars) -- unlike the older, more-cached Gayed and Bilello SSRN page this repo fetched in full for h20260923_11. The page's auto-generated 'Authors' bibliometric line (h-index 70, 17,932 citations) does not match a single-preprint tactical-allocation author and is treated as an indexer artifact, not evidence.
impact_on_spec: Confirms the primary paper exists, is dated 2025, and is a preprint (not yet peer-reviewed) -- the manifest's source_type/credibility for the mechanism is set accordingly (practitioner/preprint tier, not top-journal). Blocks any claim that this iteration read the paper's own methodology section directly; the exact-rules text in candidate-manifest.json is explicitly sourced from the AllocateSmartly and Quantitativo replications and the author's own LinkedIn abstract instead, with that substitution disclosed in search-space.md.

claim: AllocateSmartly's independent test of Carlson's Defense First paper states that at the close on the last trading day of the month, the momentum of four defensive assets (TLT, GLD, PDBC, UUP) plus a T-bill risk-free proxy (BIL) is measured as the average of each asset's 1, 3, 6 and 12-month dividend-adjusted percent return.
quote: Momentum is measured as the average of each asset’s 1, 3, 6 and 12-month dividend-adjusted % return.
limitations: Secondary source (a TAA strategy-tracking site's own restatement of the paper's rules), not the primary PDF; AllocateSmartly substitutes PDBC for the commodities leg where the author's own LinkedIn post and Quantitativo's replication both say DBC -- noted as a disclosed difference, not followed (this iteration uses DBC, matching the author's own description and local data availability).
impact_on_spec: This is the momentum-score definition pinned in candidate-manifest.json's defense_first_mechanics.momentum_score field (unweighted mean of 1M/3M/6M/12M returns) for DF01/DF02/RR-k; it is the binding constraint on warmup (12-month component needs 12 completed prior month-end closes, pinning first-valid date to 2017-01-31).

claim: AllocateSmartly states that Defense First ranks the four defensive assets from highest to lowest momentum and assigns tiered portfolio weights of 40% to the top rank, 30% to second, 20% to third, and 10% to fourth.
quote: Rank the four defensive assets from highest to lowest momentum, with portfolio allocation to each as follows: 40% (top rank), 30%, 20% and 10%.
limitations: Same secondary-source caveat as the momentum-definition claim from this page; weights confirmed consistent with the already-harvested Quantitativo/registry description (dir:defense_first_taa_carlson_concretum), which independently states the same 40/30/20/10 tiering.
impact_on_spec: Pins the exact rank-to-weight table (40/30/20/10) used by DF01, DF02 and every RR-k placebo in candidate-manifest.json; RR-k placebos keep these weights fixed and randomize only which asset receives which rank.

claim: AllocateSmartly states that if a defensive asset's momentum is less than that of T-bills, Defense First allocates that asset's tier weight to US stocks (SPY) instead -- a dual-momentum absolute-return screen applied per asset, per tier, every month.
quote: If a defensive asset’s momentum is less than that of T-bills, allocate that portion of the portfolio to US stocks (SPY).
limitations: Same secondary-source caveat; AllocateSmartly's own review separately suggests holding cash instead of UUP as an improvement they would consider, which this iteration does not adopt for DF01 (published version) but is conceptually why DF02 (SHY fallback) is preregistered as a second candidate.
impact_on_spec: Pins the paper's own fallback rule (failing tier -> SPY) as DF01 exactly; DF02 is preregistered as an explicit, disclosed departure from this rule (failing tier and the whole non-qualifying remainder -> SHY instead), not an ambiguity in the source.

claim: AllocateSmartly states that Defense First holds all positions until the end of the following month and rebalances monthly regardless of whether the target allocation has changed.
quote: Hold all positions until the end of the following month. Rebalance monthly regardless of whether there is a change in position.
limitations: AllocateSmartly does not state an explicit decision-to-fill lag (close vs next open); this iteration's manifest adds an explicit next-open fill (decision at month-end close, applied from next session open) for execution realism and consistency with the rest of this repo's cost/fill convention, disclosed as an addition beyond the source text.
impact_on_spec: Pins monthly, unconditional rebalancing (not only when ranks change) for DF01/DF02/RR-k, which is the basis for charging cost on every month-end decision date in cost-contract.json, plus any day S3's own remainder size changes intraday.

claim: Thomas Carlson's own LinkedIn announcement of the paper states the model allocates monthly across four liquid, macro-hedging ETFs (TLT, GLD, DBC, UUP) using multi-horizon momentum and an absolute strength filter, with SPY as a fallback asset.
quote: The model allocates monthly across four liquid, macro-hedging ETFs (TLT, GLD, DBC, UUP), using multi-horizon momentum and an absolute strength filter, with SPY as a fallback asset.
limitations: A promotional social-media post by the author, not the paper itself; confirms the ticker-level asset menu (DBC, not PDBC) but gives no numeric rule detail beyond what AllocateSmartly's replication already states.
impact_on_spec: This is the deciding source for using DBC (not AllocateSmartly's PDBC substitution) as the commodities leg in candidate-manifest.json, since it is the author's own description of his own paper and DBC is directly available in the local SIP daily archive (2695 bars, 2016-01-04..2026-09-22).

claim: Quantitativo's independent backtest replication of Carlson's Defense First strategy reports that, with roughly the same volatility as the S&P 500, the (3x-leveraged-fallback variant of the) strategy delivers significantly higher returns (16.2% vs. 10.6%) while maintaining a superior Sharpe ratio and much smaller drawdowns than the S&P 500 buy-and-hold benchmark.
quote: With roughly the same level of volatility as the S&P 500, the strategy now delivers significantly higher returns (16.2% vs. 10.6%) while maintaining a superior Sharpe ratio and much smaller drawdowns.
limitations: Already-harvested secondary source (registry row dir:defense_first_taa_carlson_concretum, harvested 2026-09-23, not re-read in full this pass beyond the snippet/excerpt captured in the original search); the 16.2%/10.6% figures are Quantitativo's own 3x-leveraged-fallback extension, not the paper's base unleveraged case (10.4% CAGR per the registry claim); independent from, and roughly consistent in direction with, AllocateSmartly's and BestFolio's separate replications (10.7%-11.5% CAGR ranges over longer 1971/1986-start samples).
impact_on_spec: Provides one of three independent replications (Quantitativo, AllocateSmartly, BestFolio) this iteration triangulates before trusting the mechanism is real and not one blogger's artifact; not used for any exact rule text (AllocateSmartly is used for that), only for the existing_solution_comparison narrative in direction-review.json and hypotheses.md.
